articles.title: UK police arrest five by air base under terrorism act
articles.summary: British police said counter-terrorism officers were leading efforts to establish what had happened at an airbase used by the US Royal Air Force (RAF) on Sunday, after they arrested five men on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act. The five men were also arrested on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act. US President Donald Trump told reporters they had been "looking to do big damage" at the US air base in Gloucestershire, southwest England.

articles.title: 5 arrested in U.K. near base used by U.S. on suspicion of planning terror act
articles.summary: President Trump said U.S. and British authorities were working together on the investigation. He said he believed the suspects were “looking to do big damage.”

UK: Police arrest 5 on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act
articles.summary: British police have evacuated homes near an air force base in Gloucestershire, as army bomb disposal experts examined several vehicles in what authorities described as a major incident. Five men have been arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act and offences under the Explosives Act. RAF Fairford, the base involved, is also being used by the US for strikes on Iranian missile sites targeting ships in the Strait of Hormuz. articles.title: 5 arrested for 'preparation of terror act' near RAF base used for US strikes on Iran
articles.summary: British police declared a major incident in southwest England following the arrest of several men under the Explosives Act near RAF Fairford. Military bomb disposal units inspected vehicles as emergency teams responded to the scene. The facility is used by the US Air Force for key missions. Local properties were evacuated during the investigation, Reuters reported.
